# Interstellar — relativistic flight through the Solar System

> A browser simulation of relativistic spaceflight: fly between planets at a meaningful fraction of the speed of light and watch time dilation, aberration and Doppler shift change what you see. Free, no registration. Built by Vladimir Podlevskikh (MSU physicist) as a teaching tool for special relativity.

- [Launch the simulation](https://space.podlevskikh.com/)

## The physics inside
Time dilation and the twin paradox made tangible, relativistic aberration of starlight, Doppler shift of stellar spectra, and the real scale of interplanetary distances at sub-light speeds.

- [How the physics is verified](https://space.podlevskikh.com/physics-verification.html) — the test suite, reference formulas and tolerances behind every physics claim above, honestly reported (no invented precision).
- [How far can we fly in a lifetime?](https://space.podlevskikh.com/where-we-reach.html) — interactive calculator: constant proper acceleration, flip-and-burn; distance, Earth time and peak speed for a chosen ship time, and which nearby stars are reachable.
- [Engines compared](https://space.podlevskikh.com/engines.html) — chemical, ion, nuclear-thermal, fusion (Daedalus) and solar sail on the same trip to Mars, Jupiter, Pluto, the solar gravitational lens and Alpha Centauri: flight time and delta-v for any payload (order-of-magnitude, no gravity), with cited sources.
- [Twin paradox in transit](https://space.podlevskikh.com/twins.html) — interactive round trip: how much less the travelling twin ages at constant cruise speed or under constant 1 g-class acceleration; both clocks and the world line along the way.
- [Communicating with the ship](https://space.podlevskikh.com/comms.html) — interactive: one-way and round-trip radio delay by distance (Moon, Mars, Jupiter, nearest stars incl. Proxima Centauri) and ship speed, longitudinal relativistic Doppler shift of an S/X/Ka-band carrier and the received data-rate factor; flat special relativity, radial motion only.
- [Acceleration and braking to a star](https://space.podlevskikh.com/accel.html) — interactive: flip-and-burn vs flyby at constant proper acceleration (0.01 g to 10 g) to Proxima Centauri and Barnard's Star: Earth-clock time, ship-clock time, peak speed (beta, gamma), beta(t) chart; hyperbolic motion, flat special relativity.
- [Laser sail to the nearest star](https://space.podlevskikh.com/laser-sail.html) — interactive: a ground laser pushes a mirror sail to Proxima Centauri; sliders for craft mass, laser power and sail area; relativistic dynamics with the Doppler loss of the force, diffraction-limited beam range, flight time on the Earth and craft clocks, top speed, felt acceleration, heat warning and the Newtonian estimate side by side; assumptions stated.
- [Build a mission to a star](https://space.podlevskikh.com/mission.html) — interactive mission builder: pick one of the 50 nearest stars, an engine (chemical, ion, nuclear-thermal, fusion, solar sail, laser sail, ideal photon rocket), payload mass and energy budget; returns flight time on Earth and ship clocks, total delta-v, peak speed, propellant or beam power, energy against the budget (in years of world energy use) and the share of start mass burnt on braking; sails cannot brake and the page says so; reuses the engines, laser-sail and relativistic-flight cores.
- [Interstellar dust and the shield](https://space.podlevskikh.com/dust.html) — interactive: how dangerous interstellar gas and dust are at 0.05–0.5 c; relativistic energy of one hydrogen atom (145 MeV at 0.5 c) and one dust grain (J and TNT equivalent), shield erosion along the route to any of the 50 nearest stars for a chosen medium density and shield material (graphite, beryllium, aluminium), shield thickness and mass against the craft mass with a chart over speed; an upper estimate with the model limits stated (no deflection, no secondary cascades, no crew dose); linked from the mission builder.
- [Neighbours in the galaxy](https://space.podlevskikh.com/neighbors.html) — interactive table of the 50 nearest stars and brown dwarfs: ship-clock and Earth-clock flight time at a constant proper acceleration (0.1 g to 10 g), flip-and-burn or flyby; sort by distance, spectral class or time, filter by class and distance.
- [Relativistic flight](https://space.podlevskikh.com/relativistic-flight.html) — hub page: gamma factor, ship-clock and Earth-clock time for the 10 nearest star systems at constant 1 g (flip-and-burn), and a twin-paradox clock chart for a round trip to Proxima Centauri; links to the acceleration, twin-paradox and neighbours pages.
- [Drake equation and the Fermi paradox](https://space.podlevskikh.com/drake.html) — interactive Monte-Carlo over parameter ranges (not point values): distribution of N, 16–84 % and 2.5–97.5 % intervals, probability that we are alone (N < 1), typical distance to the nearest civilisation and the chance of silence inside our radio bubble; presets (pessimist, optimist, Drake 1961, Sandberg–Drexler–Ord 2018) with a cited source per parameter; honest that fl, fi, fc, L are not measured.
- [View from the porthole](https://space.podlevskikh.com/porthole.html) — interactive sky of a pilot flying at relativistic speed toward a chosen nearby star: light aberration sweeps the 50 nearest stars forward, the Doppler effect recolours and brightens them (T' = D·T, bolometric D⁴ brightness approximation); log-scale speed slider, forward/aft view, per-star table of θ, θ', D, T'; star positions are reference values from memory, not checked against a live catalogue.
